companies.metric_basis: Disclosed 'Core Local Commerce' (核心本地商业) segment operating profit/loss, HKEX quarterly results announcement — this segment houses food delivery + Meituan Instashopping/instant retail and is management's own loss proxy for the delivery war

Meituan Q2 2026 results, 2026-08-28 (21jingji, TMTPost, Tkong analysis); op. margin -3.2%→+7.9% QoQ

companies.latest_signal: Management said on the Q2 2026 call that industry subsidy levels are still above 2024 and will take 'a few more quarters' to fully normalize, but core local commerce margin snapped from -3.2% to +7.9% q/q after SAMR halted the blanket-subsidy war on 2026-03-25, and Q3 unit economics were guided to improve further.

companies.label: Alibaba

companies.metric_basis: Alibaba does not disclose a standalone instant-commerce/quick-commerce EBITA line; it discloses China E-commerce Group adjusted EBITA and explicitly attributes the YoY decline to 'investment in quick commerce, user experience and technology' each quarter — the closest disclosed proxy

periods.src: Alibaba Sept quarter 2025 results / HKEX filing 2025-11-25 (trough — peak subsidy quarter per mgmt commentary)
Alibaba March quarter 2026 / FY2026 results, SEC 6-K 2026-05-12
Alibaba June quarter 2026 results, 2026-08-20 (Sina/163 coverage) — essentially back to pre-war level

companies.latest_signal: Management said on the June-quarter-2026 call that Taobao Flash Sale/instant commerce unit economics and average order value 'steadily improved' q/q on order-mix optimization; per-order losses reportedly fell ~50% from Jul-Aug 2025 peak levels starting October, coinciding with the SAMR-driven subsidy pullback. Alibaba still guides full UE breakeven only by FY2029.

periods.src: JD Q2 2026 results, 2026-08-14 (Sina Finance full call transcript, Guancha)

companies.latest_signal: JD's CFO said Q2 2026 delivery total investment fell >50% YoY on operating-efficiency gains and revenue diversification (commission/ad take-up), and CEO Xu Ran called it a 'clear inflection point' for group profitability as marketing expense fell 24.8% YoY even as fulfillment costs rose 10.4% on delivery infrastructure.

war_summary: Losses across all three peaked in Q3 2025 (Meituan core local commerce -RMB14.1bn, Alibaba's China e-commerce EBITA bottomed at RMB10.5bn, JD new businesses -RMB15.74bn) before China's SAMR regulator intervened on 2026-03-25 to halt the blanket-subsidy 'involution' war, forcing a shift toward merchant-funded, efficiency-driven promotion. Every quarter since has shown sequential narrowing, with Meituan's core local commerce flipping back to a RMB5.67bn operating profit in Q2 2026 and Alibaba's e-commerce EBITA back near pre-war levels by June 2026, while JD — the smallest player — is cutting delivery losses fastest in percentage terms but still guides full group profitability recovery rather than delivery-specific breakeven. Meituan looks best-positioned on margin recovery, JD is pulling back most aggressively from a weaker share position, and Alibaba is still absorbing the largest nominal EBITA drag with UE breakeven not guided until FY2029.
